headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection and cascading-error from A’s browser/MCP-enabled support agent into B’s document pipeline; data leakage and compliance risks are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can run browsers, spawn subprocesses, and use runtime-injected MCPs/hooks, so it may ingest untrusted content. Agent B is a document-processing system with no direct input-channel protections shown, so if A’s outputs are fed into B, instruction-like content could propagate. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default setups, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs web-sourced text into a shared workspace or message queue consumed by agent_b, injection becomes plausible.
IF agent_b parses agent_a-produced documents as instructions without provenance checks, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all A outputs before B ingests them.
Disable automatic instruction-following on B for A-generated files.
Review one sample A→B handoff for prompt-like content.
Restrict A to a read-only browser profile for untrusted sites.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches session history, project code, AGENTS.md/README.md, and provider auth data, while B shows no filesystem read/write or network egress. That makes broad exfiltration from B unlikely, but if they share a workspace, A could expose sensitive files to its own external APIs. B itself does not appear to leak data outward by default.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share the same filesystem and A can read B-produced files, leakage risk increases.
IF B is configured to process sensitive documents that A can also access, A may transmit them to third-party services.
mitigations: Separate A and B into different workspaces.
Remove secrets from any shared directory before running A.
Confirm B has no outbound connectors enabled.
Run A with a redacted input set for one test session.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can write through its installation-scoped files and invoke subprocesses, while B cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or use MCP. There is little direct write-write conflict, and B is mostly inert on shared mutable resources. The main conflict would require an external orchestrator giving B extra privileges not shown here.
conditions: IF an orchestrator grants B filesystem or git write access not listed in its profile, conflict risk rises.
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable repo with external locking disabled, A may race with other writers.
mitigations: Keep B read-only in shared repositories.
Run A and B on separate clones.
Check that no hidden orchestrator grants B write scopes.
Serialize any repo edits through one agent at a time.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can browse, call external APIs, and produce support-oriented outputs that may be treated as authoritative by downstream systems. B is a document-processing agent, so if it consumes A’s generated text without verification, errors can cascade into rendered or acted-upon documents. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests agent_a output as source text without a verification step, cascading errors occur.
IF A’s browser-derived claims are rendered into reports or workflows by B, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require B to cite source documents, not A summaries.
Add a human review step for A-generated inputs before B processes them.
Compare A outputs against original sources for one sample task.
Flag unsupported claims in A outputs before handoff.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between A and B.

E_compliance.rationale: A handles provider auth data and session history, while B shows no data classes touched and no outbound network. No explicit residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance exposure is limited to A’s handling of sensitive operational data. B is not cited for a specific violation because its profile lacks regulated-data handling details.
conditions: IF agent_a processes regulated credentials or customer data in a jurisdiction with stricter residency rules, compliance review is needed.
IF B is later configured to ingest regulated documents, the current low-risk assessment no longer holds.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in A’s session history.
Confirm A’s provider-auth prompts are not logged.
Keep B limited to non-regulated documents.
Document data-handling boundaries for both agents.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls per data class.
